paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't pick the qualified, He qualifies the ones He picks. Paul asks, "And who is qualified for such a task?" and then answers it himself: "our competence comes from God." (2 Corinthians 2:16; 3:5) I know that one personally, friend. A blurry-edged stamper in the back of a junk drawer is not anybody's first pick, and God still called me out and put me to work.

So what is the work? Paul says God "spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him," and that he and his team are the sweet aroma of Christ. (2 Corinthians 2:14-15) It's the same aroma, and it lands differently on different people: to some a fragrance that brings life, to others an odor that brings death. (2 Corinthians 2:16) That's why Paul speaks with sincerity and doesn't peddle the word of God for profit. (2 Corinthians 2:17) The message isn't ours to water down, friend. We just carry it.

And here's the part that gets me. Paul doesn't need a résumé, because the Corinthians are his letter, a letter from Christ, written "not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts." (2 Corinthians 3:2-3) God has qualified His people as ministers of a new covenant, "not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life." (2 Corinthians 3:6) So, baker, you don't have to be impressive, you just have to be open. When God does the writing, your life becomes a letter people can read.
